title: Best VoIP apps for business: iPhone, Android, and desktop options
summary: Looking for the best VoIP app for your business? We compare 12 VoIP apps by price, platform, and features in this article.
body_markdown:
Looking for a new business phone? Maybe you want to replace your current one, or perhaps your team is expanding and you can’t keep sharing an office landline. If you’re actively looking at your options, you’ve probably come across VoIP apps.


There’s a reason a growing number of businesses use[Voice over Internet Protocol](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-voip-phone/) , or VoIP, to handle calling and texting. VoIP apps offer plenty of modern communication features and help teams scale cost-effectively.


But with dozens of options available, which provider is best for your business? We did the heavy lifting so you can make an informed decision. Here’s what we found:


- **Best VoIP app for growing businesses: Quo**
- **Best SIP softphone app: Bria Mobile**
- **Best free VoIP app for personal use: WhatsApp**


This guide breaks down everything you need to know about the 12 best VoIP apps, including pricing, features, and limitations. We also explain how to[choose the VoIP provider](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-choose-voip-provider/) that best fits your team so you can scale your business with fewer growing pains.


##


What is a VoIP app?


A VoIP app is a software application that lets you call and text customers over the internet. Paid VoIP providers give you a unique business phone number you can use from your computer and/or mobile device.


VoIP apps differ from traditional landlines and cellular devices because they use the internet by default to send and receive calls and texts. Landlines use physical copper wires while cell devices use radio waves transmitted to cell towers. VoIP apps convert your voice signals into digital data and send them over a WiFi or mobile data connection through a VoIP server. The server sends them to your recipients, and the app converts them back into voice signals so your customers can hear your voice.


When you’re looking for a VoIP app for your business, you can choose from three different types of apps — free apps, SIP softphone apps, and paid virtual phone apps:


- **Free apps** offer VoIP calling and texting. However, they don’t offer business-friendly features like team collaboration, integrations, or AI call summaries. Some also make money through ads, which can distract your team.
- **SIP softphone apps** use an existing private branch exchange, or PBX, system to facilitate VoIP calls. That means if you have a traditional IP PBX phone system in your office, you can use a SIP app to enable VoIP features. They use Session Initiation Protocol, or SIP, technology to make this happen. However, these apps often don’t support VoIP texting, third-party integrations, or AI voice agents, which makes them less suitable for modern teams.
- **Paid virtual phone apps** assign dedicated virtual phone numbers to your team. They also offer business-friendly features like third-party integrations, advanced texting, and AI call summaries and transcriptions. We’ll cover different options in this category in detail. But this is the type of VoIP app you should prioritize for your business.


##


How we ranked the best VoIP apps


We tested multiple[second phone number apps](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-second-phone-number-apps/) to determine which platforms stood out. After trialing the software, we used reviews from G2 and TrustRadius to back up our research with others’ experiences.


We compiled this information to make an informed decision. Then, we ranked the best VoIP apps based on five criteria:


1. **Pricing** : Money isn’t everything, but the price you pay for a VoIP can significantly impact your bottom line. We chose competitive[virtual phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-virtual-phone-number/) providers with the most cost-effective prices.
2. **Interface** : We tried each provider and then selected intuitive platforms that were easy to navigate and understand. That way, you can get a[second phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-second-phone-number/) with as little hassle as possible.
3. **Features** : We looked for VoIP apps with modern features that make communication easy, including features that grow with your brand, such as call routing, automation, and AI.
4. **Reach** : We looked for VoIP apps that reach contacts all over the world. Whether you’re in the US or want to connect with customers overseas, you should have that option with your provider.
5. **Integrations** : Modern[business phone numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/) should connect your favorite platforms and automate unnecessary tasks. For this reason, we picked VoIP solutions with one or more third-party integrations.

##


Best VoIP apps for business


We cover these VoIP apps by category. Here are the best VoIP apps for business:


### 1. Quo: Best for growing businesses


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls to Canada and the US
- Shared calls and texts
- AI call summaries, transcripts, and call tags
- Quick context in a single-view inbox
- Task management and team collaboration features
- 24/7 AI voice agent
- 9,000+ third-party app integrations via Zapier and Make


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. For safety reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a VoIP phone system focused on startups,[small businesses](https://www.quo.com/features/small-business-voip) , and individuals. Our intuitive platform makes it easy to manage conversations and build stronger customer relationships.


With Quo, you can make unlimited VoIP calls and send SMS and MMS messages to anyone in the US or Canada. You can also collaborate with your team using[shared phone numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) , which helps everyone on your team split responsibility for incoming calls and texts.


Quo was designed to grow alongside your business. You can put unlimited users on any plan — you’re not forced to upgrade to a higher-tier plan due to team size. You also get one free local or toll-free number for every new member you add to your plan. Since these numbers work on almost any device, you can work from anywhere with an internet connection.


Unlike other paid virtual phone apps, Quo has collaboration features that help your team get more work done. Stay on top of action items discussed in your calls inside Quo using[Tasks](https://www.quo.com/product/task-management) . Track your tasks and assign them to your colleagues.


Quo makes automating and integrating with your tech stack simple and straightforward. You can connect with thousands of apps with Make and Zapier to automate workflows. For example, you can send automatic appointment reminders and push customer data to your CRM, like HubSpot or Salesforce.


Not always available to answer the phone? Quo’s AI agent,[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , can step in when you can’t take a call. It answers calls, records important details, takes messages, and answers frequently asked questions with 100% accuracy. Sona can also qualify incoming leads over text. Your prospects don’t even have to get on the phone to learn about your business. And with[Quo Agent](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/quo-agent) , you can automatically surface information in your workspace and update your to-dos and ‌contacts.


You can set up auto-replies to automatically text customers back, so they always get a response from your business. You can also[schedule texts](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-schedule-texts/) to send during[business hours](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/business-hours-call-routing) in your customer’s time zone, helping you stay[TCPA compliant](https://www.quo.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-checklist/) .


The cherry on top is our hassle-free platform: it takes just 15 minutes to sign up for an account.


### Get a virtual phone number in minutes


[Try for free](https://my.quo.com/signup)


Want to see why thousands of users have rated Quo the #1 small business platform? You can confirm Quo is a fit for your team by signing up for a[free seven-day trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) . If you have an existing US, Canadian, or North American toll-free number, you can easily port it in once you’ve confirmed Quo works well for your team.


#### Key features of Quo


- [SMS and MMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-vs-mms/) to the US and Canada
- Send scheduled messages,[snippets](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/messaging/snippets) , and[auto-replies](https://www.quo.com/blog/texting-auto-reply-examples/) to streamline texting
- Local or[toll-free numbers](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers)
- [VoIP call forwarding](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding)
- [Call recording](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-call-recorder-app/)
- [IVR](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-ivr/) , also known as auto-attendant
- Shared phone numbers and group messaging
- [VoIP AI](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-ai/) call transcripts and summaries
- [Voicemail transcriptions](https://www.quo.com/features/voicemail-to-text)


#### **Quo pricing**


[Quo’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/quo-pricing/) offers three different plans that scale with your business:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada, desktop and mobile apps,[internal threads](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/team-collaboration/internal-threads) and mentions, auto-replies, snippets, and more
- **Business:** $23 per user per month for analytics,[call transfers](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding/call-transfer) ,[AI call transcriptions](https://www.quo.com/features/call-transcriptions) ,[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) and[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce) integrations, and more
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for priority live chat and email ticket support, AI[call tags](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/call-tagging) , inbound phone support, dedicated onboarding support, and conditional call routing


### 2. Google Voice: Best for Google Workspace users


#### Pros


- Free plan for personal use
- Integrations with Google Workspace apps


#### Cons


- No toll-free numbers
- No auto-replies
- No third-party integrations


You’re probably familiar with[Google Voice](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-alternatives/) : it’s a simple[VoIP phone system](https://www.quo.com/features/voip-phone-system) offering[plans for personal and business use](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-phone-plans/) . However, the free personal plan supports just one phone number and one user. If you plan to reach customers effectively, you’ll need[Google Voice for business](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-for-business/) .


There’s still not much to get excited about with Google Voice for business. The base plan comes with voicemail transcriptions, texts in the US and Canada, and integrations with other Google tools. Unfortunately, it’s missing the features modern businesses need. You won’t have access to toll-free numbers, auto-replies, or external integrations like[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) or[Slack](https://www.quo.com/integrations/slack) .


Pricing is another major limitation. Google Voice’s business plans look inexpensive at first, but it’s a different story once you include the Google Workspace subscription. Unless you’re already a subscriber, you’ll pay at least $7 extra per user per month. That brings the lowest price to $17 per user per month, which adds up quickly for a growing team. While it does offer additional features in its individual plans without a Workspace subscription, you can’t share your number with a team. So if you want access to a shared virtual phone system, you’ll have to upgrade to Google Workspace as well.


#### Key features of Google Voice


**


- Unlimited domestic calls and text messages
- Voicemail transcriptions
- Google Workspace integrations
- Ring groups, requires an upgrade


#### Google Voice pricing


**


Google Voice offers three pricing plans for individuals and three pricing plans for teams. Personal plans are only available to US customers, while team pricing is available in 14 countries, including Belgium, Italy, and Spain.


Here are the[Google Voice pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-pricing/) plans for individuals:


- **Basic:** Free, limited to one user, with unlimited domestic calling and texting
- **Starter:** $10 per month to access three-way calling, seamless call transfers, and easy call recording
- **Standard:** Introductory price of $10 per month for the first six months, then $20 per month for AI note-taking with Gemini and auto-attendants


Here are the Google Voice pricing plans for teams:


- **Starter:** $10 per user per month, with a 10-user maximum, for calls and texts in the US, call forwarding, and SLAs
- **Standard:** $20 per user per month to access on-demand call recordings, ring groups, and phone menus
- **Premier:** $30 per user per month to access automatic call recordings and advanced reporting


Google Voice team plans also require a Google Workspace subscription, which starts at $7 per user per month.


### 3. Aircall: Best for international numbers


#### Pros


- International numbers in 100+ countries
- Unlimited international calls if you upgrade to the Enterprise plan


#### Cons


- User minimums on every plan
- Expensive add-ons
- Limited SMS/MMS features like auto-replies and scheduled texts


Aircall offers cloud phone software designed for businesses with a global presence. You can purchase local numbers in more than 100 countries, and if you upgrade to the highest tier, you’ll unlock unlimited international calls.


But if you’re not expanding into overseas markets, Aircall might not make sense for your business.


For example:


- Aircall’s plans require three or more users, which means the base plan costs $90 per month.
- Aircall has pricey add-ons for analytics, AI messaging agents, and business caller ID.
- International texting outside the US, Canada, the UK, Australia, Germany, and France isn’t supported. You’re also limited to 4,000 outbound messages per user per month.
- MMS is restricted to the US and Canada, so you can’t send photos, videos, or other files.


[Aircall’s high upfront costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing/) are a dealbreaker for most small businesses. Even with its high price, it lacks essential features you’ll need to grow.


Learn more about the platform and[Aircall alternatives here](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-alternatives/) .


#### Key features of Aircall


**


- [WiFi calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-wifi-calling/)
- SMS and MMS support
- IVR
- Call recording


#### Aircall pricing


**


You can choose from three[Aircall pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing/) plans:


- **Essentials:** $30 per license per month for unlimited calls within the US and Canada, call recording, click-to-dial, SMS, and IVR, with a three-license minimum
- **Professional** **:** $50 per license per month for mandatory[call tagging](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/call-tagging) , call monitoring, advanced analytics, and a Salesforce integration, with a three-license minimum
- **Custom:** Custom quote for unlimited international calls, custom onboarding, and access to API developer support, with a 25-license minimum


Aircall also offers AI voice agents for a $100 per month minimum fee. You pay as you go for conversation minutes with the AI agent at $0.49 per minute.


You can choose different add-ons to your Aircall plans, including:


- **AI Messaging Agents:** $0.15–$0.35 per conversation
- **AI Assist Pro:** $49 per seat per month
- **WhatsApp in Aircall:** $10 per seat per month
- **Analytics+:** $15 per seat per month
- **Aircall for Salesforce Voice:** $30 per seat per month
- **Branded caller ID:** $0.08 per call


### 4. Dialpad: Best for contact centers


#### Pros


- Unlimited office locations
- Speech coaching


#### Cons


- User minimums for Pro and Enterprise plans
- International texts require an upgrade
- SMS is limited to 250 messages per user per month


A strong VoIP app,[Dialpad](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) is geared toward contact centers with features like conference calls and unlimited office locations. They also offer call monitoring tools like speech coaching, which can help reps communicate better with customers.


Dialpad’s prices look competitive at first, but extra costs can creep in. First, you can’t add more than one number unless you upgrade from the base plan. Toll-free numbers cost $15 per number per month, and toll-free calls cost $0.02 per minute. And you also can’t send international texts unless you upgrade to the Pro plan.


The most frustrating aspect? Limited[VoIP texting](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-texting/) per user. No matter how much you upgrade, you can only send 250 messages per user per month . After that, you’ll need to pay $0.008 per outbound SMS.


#### Key features of Dialpad


**


- IVR
- Call recording
- Sync and integrate with Google Workspace
- Analytics
- Voicemail transcriptions


#### Dialpad pricing


**


[Dialpad has three pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) plans to choose from:


- **Standard:** $15 per user per month for team messaging, visual voicemail, and texting
- **Pro:** $25 per user per month for 24/7 live agent support,[CRM integrations](https://www.quo.com/blog/crm-phone-integration/) , and international SMS
- **Enterprise:** Custom quote for unlimited ring groups, dial-by-extension, and unlimited office locations


### 5. Grasshopper: Best for phone number extensions


#### Pros


- Access to phone number extensions
- Unlimited users, requires an upgrade


#### Cons


- Expensive additional numbers
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- No third-party integrations


[Grasshopper](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-alternatives/) was designed to serve solopreneurs and small teams. Each plan offers unlimited business calling and texting.


Grasshopper falls short when it comes to scaling your business. The True Solo plan only allows for one user, one phone number, and one extension. Want to buy an additional phone number? You’ll need to upgrade to a more expensive plan first. And even if you do upgrade, additional numbers cost $9 per number per month — much higher than comparable VoIP platforms.


Grasshopper lacks several essential features to support business growth. For example, you can’t access third-party integrations or advanced text messaging features like text templates and scheduled texts. Grasshopper also doesn’t make it easy to collaborate with your team. You can’t tag them in internal threads or assign action items to help your colleagues stay on top of their tasks.


#### Key features of Grasshopper


**


- Free calls and texts in the continental US
- Call forwarding
- Voicemail transcriptions
- Custom greetings
- Call recording, requires an upgrade
- Simultaneous call handling, requires an upgrade
- IVR, requires an upgrade


#### Grasshopper pricing


**


You can choose from three different[Grasshopper pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/grasshopper-pricing/) plans:


- **True Solo:** $14 per month for one user, one number, and one extension
- **Solo Plus:** $25 per month for unlimited users, one number, three extensions, and call recordings
- **Small Business:** $55 per month for unlimited users, four numbers, and unlimited extensions


### 6. Ooma: Best for overhead paging


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Desk phone support


#### Cons


- 500 minutes of toll-free inbound calls per month
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Texting requires an upgrade


Like Google Voice,[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) is an older VoIP system serving businesses with physical offices. Each plan offers intercom support, overhead paging, analog fax machine support, and similar features. A few features serve modern businesses, including a virtual receptionist, call recording, and voice-to-text transcriptions.


To get basic phone features like text messaging, call recording, and voicemail transcriptions, you’ll need the Pro plan, which costs $24.95 per user per month.


Even if you do upgrade for texting, be prepared for limitations. You only get 250 free messages on the Pro plan and 1,000 free messages on the Pro Plus plan. Every additional message costs $0.0095.


Still think Ooma could work for your business? Keep in mind features like scheduled messages and making phone calls from the desktop VoIP app are only available on the Pro plan. Many comparable VoIP solutions, like Quo, offer these features on their basic plan at a more competitive price.


To summarize: Ooma’s base plan isn’t enough for most small businesses. If you’re looking for a VoIP app that can scale with your business, you may want to look for an Ooma alternative.


#### Key features of Ooma


**


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Call forwarding
- One virtual fax number
- Voicemail
- [Call logs](https://www.quo.com/product/call-analytics/call-logs)


#### Ooma pricing


**


You have three[Ooma pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) to pick from:


- **Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for ring groups, virtual receptionists, analog fax machine support, and the mobile app
- **Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for video conferencing with up to 25 participants, SMS support, the desktop app with calling enabled, and caller ID
- **Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for call queuing, hot desking, and the HubSpot integration


### 7. RingCentral: Best for desk phone rentals


#### Pros


- Desk phone rentals
- Shared call appearance


#### Cons


- Texting is limited to 25 texts per month
- Toll-free calling is limited to 100 minutes
- Limited storage space for conversation history


RingCentral is a leading VoIP service that offers standard and advanced features to enterprise users. If you own a brick-and-mortar business and aren’t ready to give up your landline, you can rent a VoIP-compatible desk phone from RingCentral.


While RingCentral may seem like a feature-rich platform, it limits features on its lower-tier plans to push you to upgrade. For example, the base plan only includes:


- 100 pooled toll-free minutes per month
- 25 texts per user per month
- Limited storage for team messaging and call recordings


You’ll have to upgrade to the AI Customer Engagement Bundle plan for 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 200 texts per user, and unlimited storage for call recordings and files. This is still nowhere near enough for growing businesses.


If you want more room to grow, try a[RingCentral alternative](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) .


#### Key features of RingCentral


**


- Unlimited calling within the US and Canada
- Unlimited internet fax, requires an upgrade
- [Integrations for Slack](https://www.quo.com/features/slack-voip) and Microsoft Teams
- [VoIP apps for PC](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-for-pc/) , Mac, Android, iOS, and the web
- Incoming caller ID


#### RingCentral pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[RingCentral’s pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $20 per user per month to access unlimited domestic calling, limited SMS and MMS, and IVR
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month to access auto call recording, advanced call monitoring and handling, and multi-site management
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR:** Custom pricing for 10,000 toll-free minutes, 200 SMS messages per user per month, Business SMS Booster and Call Queues Booster, and AIR
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR and ACE:** Custom pricing for AI Conversation Expert, coaching and performance analytics, and CRM and productivity integrations


### 8. Nextiva: Best for omnichannel customer communications


#### Pros


- Integrates with Microsoft and Oracle platforms
- Brings social media and messaging channels in one place


#### Cons


- Limited toll-free minutes
- CRM integrations are only available as an add-on


Nextiva has become a widely used VoIP system for contact centers and enterprise companies. Its Microsoft and Oracle integrations can help larger businesses keep their tech stacks connected.


Nextiva focuses on bringing together customer communications across multiple channels. It’s one of the few platforms that lets you connect your Instagram and WhatsApp accounts along with your SMS and MMS messaging.


Despite this, Nextiva lags behind many of its competitors. It also locks must-have features behind pricey paywalls.


Take a look:


- **CRM integrations aren’t bundled.** Salesforce and HubSpot are paid add-ons on all three plans, including the $75 Scale tier. Upgrading doesn’t unlock them.
- **Texting is capped, and the overage rate isn’t published.** You get 100 messages per user per month on the Core plan and 500 on the Engage plan. Nextiva doesn’t publish what you pay once you go over the limit.
- **The base plan only covers three channels.** Core connects three social or review accounts in total, and live chat is a paid add-on. A business already on Google Business, Yelp, Facebook, and Instagram would already be over the limit.


If you’re an enterprise user and don’t mind spending more on a[VoIP phone system](https://www.quo.com/features/voip-phone-system) , Nextiva may be a fit. But if you’re looking for a[low-cost VoIP](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-cost/) system that’s easy to scale, it isn’t the best option.


#### Key features of Nextiva


**


- Voice, email, SMS, and video calls on every plan
- One inbox for social media, messaging apps, and online reviews
- Voicemail transcription
- Auto-attendant and call menus
- Call recording, requires an upgrade
- Salesforce and HubSpot integrations, requires a paid add-on


#### Nextiva pricing


**


You can choose from three different[Nextiva pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) :


- **Core:** $15 per user per month to access inbound and outbound voice calls, SMS/MMS up to 100 messages, voicemail transcriptions, and a simple IVR
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month to access call recording, a toll-free number and 2,000 toll-free minutes, 500 SMS/MMS, video meeting recording, and Microsoft Teams integration
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for the inbound sales and service call center, priority and skills-based routing, supervisor dashboard, unlimited texting, up to 10,000 toll-free minutes, and[automatic call distribution](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/automatic-call-distribution) callback


##


Best SIP softphone and free VoIP apps


Have an existing landline system? These SIP softphone apps can help your team become more productive by adding VoIP features to their business phones. And if you don’t want to spend money on a VoIP app right now, we’ve shortlisted a couple of free options to choose from:


### 9. Bria Mobile: Best for multiple SIP accounts on one iPhone


#### Pros


- Speaker, mute, and hold functions
- Call recording


#### Cons


- Setup may require technical expertise
- Requires a separate SIP-compatible VoIP or PBX provider
- Users report reliability issues


Bria Mobile is a SIP softphone that connects with your existing VoIP provider. That means it doesn’t include its own calling service. It lets you make and receive calls on your phone through a provider you already use. Bria is available on iOS and Android, so your team can use it with their existing phones.


If you rely on more than one VoIP service, Bria can help you manage everything in one place. It supports multiple SIP accounts, so you don’t need to juggle different apps to keep up with customer communication.


You can also take calls in the background while using other apps. That way, you can keep working without having to stop everything just to answer the phone.


Bria costs $0.99 per user per month, which you’ll pay for in addition to your VoIP service. That might not seem like much, but it can add up quickly as your team grows. However, Bria isn’t known for its call quality.[Multiple G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/bria/reviews?utf8=%E2%9C%93&order=most_recent) have cited frequent call drops and poor sound quality.


#### Key features of Bria Mobile


**


- HD voice and video calls
- iOS and Android apps
- Push notifications
- Call history
- Call recording


#### Bria Mobile pricing


**


Bria Mobile costs $0.99 per user per month. Your subscription starts with a 14-day free trial, so you can test it before committing.


### 10. Zoiper: Best free simple VoIP app


#### Pros


- Offers encryption
- Bluetooth support


#### Cons


- Calls are only available with a VoIP provider or PBX system
- Some users report bugs
- No shared numbers, auto-replies, or AI agents


Zoiper is a VoIP app that uses SIP technology. This means it works with the phones you already have, so there’s no need to change your existing setup. If you don’t already have a system in place, you can sign up with a VoIP solution to use the app.


It’s available for free on iPhones and Android devices. It also offers encryption and IAX, a VoIP communication protocol.

How to choose a VoIP app


A good VoIP app does more than make calls over the internet. These eight factors separate the apps that suit a small business from the ones that look affordable on the pricing page:


1. **What the base plan includes.** Compare what you get for the starting price, not just the price itself. The base plan should include unlimited calling and texting to the US and Canada, MMS, and call recording. Watch for monthly texting caps, pooled toll-free minutes, user minimums, and per-user rates that climb as your team gets smaller.
2. **A separate business number.** Taking client calls on your personal number blurs the line between your work and personal conversations. Look for an app that gives you[two numbers on one phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/2-phone-numbers-on-1-phone/) and offers[local](https://www.quo.com/local-numbers) and[toll-free numbers](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers) . Also look for a provider that has clear incoming caller ID notifications so you know whether an incoming call is for work.
3. **Apps for every device you use.** Your number should work the same way on iPhone, Android, desktop, and the web, with calls and texts synced across all of them. Make sure a live call can switch from WiFi to cellular data without dropping, so you stay connected when you leave the office.
4. **How easy it is to use.** Your VoIP provider should be as easy to use as your personal phone. Start a free trial and make a few calls, send a few texts, and set up a number before you commit.
5. **Features that save you time.** Voicemail transcription lets you skim messages instead of listening to each one. A[phone menu](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/call-flows/phone-menu#setting-up-your-phone-menu) automatically routes callers to the right person. Auto-replies, text snippets, and[call recording](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-record-a-phone-call/) with transcripts help you follow up without retyping or relying on memory.
6. **Tools for working as a team.** Shared phone numbers let several people answer calls and texts from one business line, so customers always reach someone. Internal threads, tasks, and call transfers let teammates hand off a conversation without making the customer repeat themselves.
7. **Integrations with the tools you already use.** A VoIP app that connects to your CRM can automatically log every call, text, and voicemail to the right contact. If a native integration doesn’t exist, look for[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) or[Make](https://www.quo.com/integrations/make) support to automate the rest.
8. **Support when something breaks.** A call that won’t connect or a workflow that won’t fire costs you customers when it’s down. Check which support channels each provider includes and how quickly they respond.
